💡Energy access creates opportunities: for better education, access to health services and meaningful work - to name a few.
And yet 675 million people still lack access to electricity, trapped in cycles of poverty and inequality that disproportionately impact women and girls. 
🌎 UNDP is committed to change that leaves no one behind, and with our partners at IBM 's Sustainability Accelerator, we’ve spent the last 18 months working on two tech-driven solutions:  
📍 Clean Electricity Equity Index (CEEI) 
📍 Forecasting Electricity Access (FEA) 
On 09 April we’re kicking off a #globalconsultation to explore these tools and make them better – and we need your help.
🚀 Join ourlaunch webinar with UNDP ’s Marcos Neto and IBM ’s Justina Nixon-Saintil . Learn more about our ambition, how we've designed these tools, and from leaders working on the frontlines of development.

repost-ee9d1c4eab0d0c00a98a.sharedText:
I am absolutely honored to be selected as an IRENA Youth Delegate for 2024. 
 
I am thrilled to be among the 100 IRENA Youth Delegates from 60 different countries, The New Generation of Decision Makers at the International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA)  Youth Forum at the 14th IRENA Assembly in Abu Dhabi, UAE. 
The program kicked off with a welcoming session led by the Director-General of IRENA and esteemed guests, followed by panel discussions covering various topics focused on fostering engagement in key technological advancements, building capacity for #youth at the core of the energy transition, providing #opportunities for youth to play a key role in #IRENA's mission of accelerating #renewableenergy deployment, achieving climate objectives, and advancing the #sustainable development agenda.

Over the first days of the forum, we had an enlightening introduction on topics in #finance, #science, #social, and #policy aspects in renewable energy. We had presentation about introduction to renewable energy by Cesar Barraza-Botet, PhD  covering renewable energy sources from solar to wind, hydrogen, and new innovations in the sector. Other sessions included skills development for the energy transition by Samah Elsayed, discussions on ESGs and Social Corporate Responsibility for a just energy transition by AbdelRahman Fahmy  and Asma Rouabhia, and skills youth need in developing renewable energy projects and proposals by AbdelRahman Fahmy and David Arinze 

On the second day of the forum, I attended the session with IEEE , Advancing Technology for Humanity works on #AI for #DigitalInnovations in Energy transitions with speakers Sajith Wijesuriya, Krishna Ajith  and  Cybele Ghanem.    

The Forum continued with a panel discussion including #AcceleratingYouthLedInnovationandEntrepreneurshipinCleanTechPanel, with panelists, Grace Nanteza, Asma Rouabhia, Nourhan Algharabli, Benjamin Keller  and Shreshth Mishra, who shared the challenges and barriers faced by youth-led innovations. 

There inspiring thoughts, experiences, and advice addressed the true skills that all young changemakers  need to have, emphasizing the importance of being ready to #failfast, Having the #courage to continue until we achieve success as well as creating as many #connections as possible. 
I had the opportunity to share about renewable energy projects to  powering agriculture and the potential of #Agrivoltaics,  integrating the  #food production and #energy generation, the Food-Energy-Water nexus.  

The IRENA Youth Forum were filled with #encouragement with inspirational closing by from Riccardo Toxiri and Riad Meddeb.  I look forward to the #IRENAAssembly and the #FutureEnergyForum in the coming days which IRENA Youth delegates have the opportunity to meet with global leaders, government representatives, and IRENA experts.

#IRENA #RenewableEnergy #YouthLeadership #SDGs  #Sustainability #ClimeteAction  #YouthEmpowerment  #EnergyTransition #EnergyEfficiency

Reflecting on an enriching week in Abu Dhabi at the 14th Assembly #IRENA14A, where I engaged with brilliant minds, exchanged perspectives, and championed solutions BY and FOR the youth.

🤝 bi-laterals 🤝

Grateful for bilateral meetings with leaders like H.E Philippe Henry Minister of Climate, Energy and Mobility of Government of Wallonia 🇧🇪 who brought invaluable insights regarding the strategy adopted in Belgium. 
Discussions with Sandra Dickison Deputy Director at the U.S. Department of Energy 🇺🇸, and Dr. Martin Keller President of the Global Alliance for Sustainable Energy  were truly enlightening regarding the role of R&D and research to advance the best practices.

⭕️Youth circle ⭕️ 

Honored to engage with visionaries like H.E. Dr Amani Abou-Zeid أماني أبوزيد Commissioner of Energy at the African Union 🌍, and Dr. Nawal Al-Hosany, UAE's Permanent Representative to IRENA, who put the spotlight on the importance of critical thinking.

🗣️ Fireside chat 🗣️

Fireside chats with H.E Dr. Amna bint Abdullah Al Dahak  UAE's Minister of Climate Change and Environment 🇦🇪 and 
Mr. Riad Meddeb UNDP’s Sustainable Energy Hub Director, highlighted the vital role of education, engagement and active participation in the energy sector.

Meeting His Excellency Dr. Dr. Sultan Al Jaber, CEO ADNOC Group, President COP28 UAE, Chairman Masdar (Abu Dhabi Future Energy Company), and Minister of Industry and Advanced Technology for UAE, was no less than a dream come true! Last week, I had the incredible honour of serving as the official Youth Representative at the International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA) (A United Nations Organisation) Youth Forum: The New Generation of Decision Makers, the IRENA 14th Assembly, and the World Future Energy Summit in Abu Dhabi. 

Throughout these events, I engaged with diplomats, ministers, and policymakers from across the globe, discussing the challenges and opportunities in the transition to sustainable energy. It was enlightening to see the world come together with a shared goal of fostering a cleaner, more sustainable future. Moderating a live session and questioning Riad Meddeb, Director of Sustainability Hub, United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), about bridging the gap between youth, financing, and renewable energy was one of the major highlights.

I was particularly inspired by the diversity and passion of the other youth delegates—over 150 of us chosen from a pool of 57,000 applicants. Together, we exchanged ideas, learned from one another, and advocated for the integration of youth perspectives in shaping global energy policies.

The insights gained and the connections made have profoundly impacted my understanding of global energy dynamics. I am grateful for the opportunity to represent youth interests at such a high level and am more committed than ever to contributing to our sustainable future.

¡La 4ta Conferencia de Pequeños Estados Insulares en Desarrollo comienza hoy! 

Para los PEID, el modelo energético tradicional simplemente no es sostenible. El aumento de los costos del combustible afecta a las economías, la quema de combustibles fósiles amenaza los ecosistemas interconectados, y la dependencia de las importaciones de combustible extranjero crea vulnerabilidades climáticas y comerciales.

En esta línea, ya está disponible la Edición Especial del Boletín de UNDP Sustainable Finance Hub , donde se discuten las enormes posibilidades de construir un desarrollo sostenible en estos países mediante la transformación de sus sistemas energéticos.
